title: Adversarial examples for heuristics in combinatorial optimization: An LLM based approach

mechanism.domainTask: Adversarial-instance generation for combinatorial optimization heuristics
mechanism.populationDetail: A global undivided database of executable Python programs, each representing an adversarial instance generator.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The scored database contains all valid programs while high-scoring programs are emphasized as best programs; no separate bounded archive is specified.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The database grows when executable programs are added; Co-FunSearch also reinjects manually simplified programs.
mechanism.generationDetail: One sampled program is supplied as the editable source and the LLM requests a similar program with improved score.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Executable validity and problem-specific score metadata are stored and reused for database sampling and best-program inspection.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The database sampling distribution and exact score-to-probability rule are delegated to FunSearch and not exposed; high-score programs are emphasized.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Human-in-the-loop simplification and reinjection of high-scoring programs is outside the current automated taxonomy; implicit high-score archive status is a boundary case.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/ADVERSARIAL EXAMPLES FOR HEURISTICS IN COMBINATORIAL OPTIMIZATION AN LLM BASED APPROACH.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Current survey placement emphasizes adversarial-instance applications and human collaboration, but does not clearly cite all matching mechanism sections; exact archive semantics, prompt text, and database sampling probabilities are only partly exposed.
